The first release of Tafrigh: transcripts of Egyptian Arabic–English meetings and calls, made on your
own computer, with each speaker told apart by voice.

## Download

- Windows 10 and 11: `Tafrigh-0.1.0-setup.exe` installs for your user, without admin rights. It isn't
  signed yet, so SmartScreen warns about an unknown publisher: choose *More info*, then *Run anyway*.
- Linux (x64): unpack `Tafrigh-0.1.0-linux-x64.tar.gz` and run `Tafrigh/Tafrigh`.
- `SHA256SUMS.txt` has the checksums of both.

On first start, open *Settings → Models on this computer* and download a model: Cohere Transcribe
Arabic (1.6 GB) or the whisper-medium code-switching model (778 MB).

## What's in it

- Three local models: Cohere Transcribe Arabic (13.4% word error rate on the Egyptian test set), the
  whisper-medium code-switching fine-tune (18.5%, keeps 90% of English terms in English), and Whisper
  large-v3 with an Egyptian style hint.
- ElevenLabs Scribe and Speechmatics with your own API key; the recording is uploaded only after you
  confirm.
- Speaker labels by voice (TitaNet-small voiceprints), with the number of people given or estimated.
- The graphics card is used when it helps: Cohere on any GPU through Vulkan (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel),
  Whisper on NVIDIA GPUs after a one-click download of NVIDIA's libraries.
- Playback in step with the text, search, renaming and merging speakers, editing lines, and exports
  to text, SRT, WebVTT, Markdown and JSON.
- Settings for power mode, processor threads and the graphics card, and speed estimates that learn
  from earlier runs on your computer.

## Known limits

- Local transcripts are drafts: on real meetings they differed from ElevenLabs on 44–49% of the words.
- Whisper on CUDA hasn't run on a real NVIDIA card yet; it falls back to the processor if anything
  fails.
- The installer is unsigned, there are no automatic updates, and macOS isn't built.

The notes behind the numbers are in the [project docs](https://github.com/MohammedEl-sayedAhmed/arabic-stt/tree/main/docs).
